clue.text: Victory by a five-point score producing no cheer

parts.note: a victory is a win
in rugby union a try scores five points

explanation.surface: A rugby match won by a single try leaves the crowd unmoved.
explanation.walkthrough: A TRY, worth five points in rugby union, is the 'five-point score'; 'by' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Wintry weather or a wintry smile is bleak and cheerless, giving no comfort.

clue.text: Refuse to give description of cargo boat

definitions.meaning: to hold something back and not hand it over
a cargo boat is a vessel equipped with a hold, so it is the answer

explanation.surface: Someone declines to describe a freighter.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into WITH HOLD: a cargo ship comes with a hold for its goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To withhold is to keep back or decline to give something asked for.

clue.text: Nettles, not wanted, cut down

indicators.note: a word cut down loses its final letter, here the tail of the word for unwanted

parts.note: something not wanted is needless

explanation.surface: Unwanted stinging plants are hacked back in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nettles' looks like the plants, but here it is a verb meaning irritates. 'cut down' removes the last S from NEEDLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone and to nettle them both mean to irritate or provoke them.

clue.text: Novel hero gives bird girl's name

parts.note: the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend
Hester is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A fictional hero apparently names a bird after a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives' is a link word joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Rochester is the brooding hero of Charlotte Brontë's novel Jane Eyre.

clue.text: Clamber's another way to put it

definitions.text: Clamber's another way to put it

indicators.note: putting the letters another way means rearranging them into a new order

parts.note: the word with its apostrophe-s gives eight letters to shuffle

explanation.surface: A remark that a synonym for clamber could be offered.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does two jobs: the answer is a rearrangement of the letters of CLAMBER'S, and it is also another word for clamber.
explanation.definitionFit: To scramble up a slope is to clamber, climbing awkwardly on hands and feet.

clue.text: Cataloguing of raincoat it goes astray

indicators.note: letters gone astray have wandered out of their order, so they must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A clothing inventory where a raincoat has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' rearranges RAINCOAT IT GOES, fourteen letters; 'goes' reads as the verb but is fodder, and 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cataloguing things means sorting them into classes, which is what categorisation is.

clue.text: A woman going by name of Tree

parts.note: she refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A woman goes by the surname Tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going by' is a link word; 'of Tree' defines an adjective meaning made of or relating to the ash tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen as an adjective can mean made from or relating to ash wood, the tree.

clue.text: One after another, say, put your teeth into jars

indicators.note: say tells you the answer is what this phrase sounds like when spoken

parts.note: to put your teeth into is to bite, and jars are urns

explanation.surface: Someone describes biting into pots in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals that BITE URNS, spoken, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things by turns means alternately, one following another.

clue.text: Alex — he is unlikely to expire

indicators.note: an unlikely form of these words is an improbable rearrangement of them

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Alex is apparently in good health and not about to die.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is unlikely' rearranges ALEX HE; 'expire' means breathe out, not die.
explanation.definitionFit: To expire in its literal sense is to breathe out, which is to exhale.

clue.text: Promising cover for head

parts.note: read as a headland full of optimism: a cape covers a head, and good hope is promising

explanation.surface: An encouraging hat or hood.
explanation.walkthrough: A cape is also a headland, and 'promising' suggests good hope; the whole clue describes a famous South African headland.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous headland near the tip of Africa bears a name that literally means a promontory of optimism.

clue.text: "Excavation" — a set of books vigorous in style

parts.note: a trench is a dug excavation
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Review of a digging manual praising its forceful prose.
explanation.walkthrough: NT, the New Testament, is a set of books in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant writing is incisive and forceful, cutting to the point vigorously.

clue.text: Draw fine lines to represent opening

definitions.meaning: in drawing, to shade with closely spaced parallel lines
a small door or aperture, as in a ship's deck

explanation.surface: Some cross-shading represents a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to represent' is the link between two separate senses of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: shading with fine lines, and a trapdoor-like opening.

clue.text: Greek man embracing woman

indicators.note: the first piece wraps its arms around the second, holding it inside

parts.note: he refers to a man
Ellen is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A Greek man hugs a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek man' reads as a unit, but 'Greek' alone is the definition and 'man' is HE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hellene is a Greek, the Greeks' own name for themselves.

clue.text: Leader is not specific

definitions.meaning: broad or applying overall rather than in detail

explanation.surface: A head of state speaks only in vague terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' links two senses: a military leader, and an adjective meaning broad.
explanation.definitionFit: An army commander holds that rank, and broad, non-specific statements are described that way too.

clue.text: Catalogue covering unknown composer

indicators.note: the first piece covers the second by enclosing it

parts.note: a catalogue is a list
in algebra Z is an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A catalogue of works by an unidentified composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Mathematicians use x, y and z for unknowns, so 'unknown' is Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian Romantic composer and piano virtuoso.

clue.text: Expect crew's quarters to be reduced by 20%

indicators.note: being reduced by an amount means that portion is taken away from the word

parts.note: the forecastle is the forward part of a ship where the crew live
a fifth of a ten-letter word is two letters, taken here from its end

explanation.surface: Sailors anticipate cramped quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: FORECASTLE has ten letters; dropping 20% leaves eight.
explanation.definitionFit: To forecast is to predict, which means expecting something in advance.

clue.text: Conservative heading in the right direction for crowd

parts.note: on course means heading the right way

explanation.surface: A Tory politician steering a crowd the right way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse is a gathering or throng of people, a crowd.

clue.text: Discard counter one's found inside

indicators.note: the second piece is located within the first

parts.note: a jetton is a counter or token used in games
one is I, and 's is short for is

explanation.surface: A gaming chip found inside is thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: A jetton is a counter used in games; 'one's' gives I + S, the 's standing for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison something is to throw it away or discard it.

clue.text: Forged acknowledgement of debt accepted by football club

indicators.note: the second piece is taken into the first

parts.note: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur football club
an IOU acknowledges a debt

explanation.surface: A fake IOU is accepted by a football club.
explanation.walkthrough: SPURS is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spurious is fake or counterfeit, as a forged document is.

clue.text: Place in France — its description shows some deficiency

parts.note: Pau is a city in south-west France
Pau is a city, so city describes it

explanation.surface: A French town whose description reveals a lack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows some' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A paucity is a scarcity or lack, a deficiency in number or amount.

clue.text: Steel never breaks

indicators.note: a word that breaks falls apart and its letters reassemble

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Steel is said to be unbreakable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steel' seems a noun for metal, but is courage; 'breaks' rearranges NEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To steel yourself is to summon courage, and nerve is courage or boldness.

clue.text: Mischievous behaviour that's understood around start of university year

indicators.note: the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: roger is the radio reply meaning message received and understood

indicators.note: start of takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Pranks that are tolerated at the beginning of the university year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's understood' gives ROGER, the radio reply; 'around' puts it round U ('start of university'), then Y follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Roguery is playful mischief as well as dishonesty.

clue.text: Book is first class, a humdinger from the very start

parts.note: A1 means first class, written AI in crosswords

indicators.note: the very start of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A book praised as excellent, a real humdinger from page one.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first class) is written AI, the digit 1 read as letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaiah is a book of the Old Testament, named after the prophet.

clue.text: Group of soldiers — about 51 — run down

indicators.note: the first piece sits about the second, surrounding it

parts.note: a squad is a small group of soldiers
LI is 51 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An army squad of around fifty-one men is exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about 51' looks like an approximate headcount of soldiers, but 'about' is the container signal and 51 is a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A squalid, run-down place is dirty and neglected.

clue.text: A measure of alcohol — it represents a small proportion

indicators.note: a small proportion of these words is a short run of their letters taken from inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A drinks statistic claiming alcohol makes up only a tiny share.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'a small proportion' as the definition, but a litre is no proportion: 'A measure' defines, 'of' is a link, and 'represents a small proportion' marks the hidden run in alcohoL IT REpresents.
explanation.definitionFit: A litre is a metric unit for measuring volume.

clue.text: Musing, despite the fact that time's short

parts.note: though means despite the fact that
time in its short form is the abbreviation T

explanation.surface: Daydreaming even though time is running out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time's short' looks like urgency, but means time abbreviated, T.
explanation.definitionFit: Thought is musing or reflection, the act of thinking something over.

clue.text: Mug — I had one to put back

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: putting a word back means writing it in reverse

explanation.surface: Someone admits being a fool for returning a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' reverses TO to OT.
explanation.definitionFit: A mug in British slang is a fool or gullible person, an idiot.

clue.text: Old and obstinate, Leslie is not using scent

parts.note: dour means stern and obstinate
Les is short for Leslie
is contracts to 's

explanation.surface: An old, stubborn man called Leslie refuses to wear aftershave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leslie is' becomes LES'S: Les for Leslie, with 'is' shortened to 's.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not wearing scent gives off no smell, which is to be odourless.

clue.text: Coward's allergic reaction

definitions.meaning: a comedy by Noël Coward, the English playwright
an allergy to pollen causing sneezing

explanation.surface: A timid person's allergic flare-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coward' looks like a timid person; it is the playwright Noël Coward, whose 1925 comedy bears this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Noël Coward wrote a comedy with this title, and it is also the common pollen allergy.

clue.text: African range American found short

parts.note: ken is the range of one's knowledge

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a Yank is an American

explanation.surface: An African mountain range found by an American to be lacking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' suggests mountains but is KEN, range of knowledge; 'short' trims YANK to YAN. 'found' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kenyan is a person from Kenya, an African country.
